extracted.intended_audience: respondents, petitioners, trade attorneys, and Department of Commerce staff involved in antidumping investigations
extracted.subtask_description: Department of Commerce positions and procedural standards for determining price, constructed value (CV), cost of manufacture (COM), adjustments, verification, and related evidentiary matters in antidumping investigations of large, custom-made capital equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of purchase price (reported U.S. price)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purchase price based on packed, ex-go down, Japanese port prices or packed, f.o.b., U.S. port prices, as appropriate. Deductions made, where appropriate, for foreign inland freight and insurance, ocean freight; brokerage and handling, stevedoring charges, marine insurance, air freight, U.S. Customs duty and fees, and installation supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make appropriate deductions to arrive at comparable ex-factory or export price; see DOC Position to Comment 3 for treatment of accessory items and installation supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructed Value (CV) components
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructed value includes materials, fabrication, general expenses, profit, and packing pursuant to section 773(e) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use actual general expenses if they exceed statutory minimum; apply statutory minimum profit (eight percent) where appropriate; include imputed credit costs in home market selling expenses; home market selling expenses used per section 773(e)(1)(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of actual general expenses vs statutory minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual general expenses were used when they exceeded the statutory minimum requirement of ten percent of materials and fabrication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer to use company-specific actual G&A when it reasonably reflects costs; otherwise statutory minima apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory minimum profit application
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory eight percent minimum profit was applied in the constructed value calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply statutory profit floor when company-specific profit data do not justify a different amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of imputed credit costs in selling expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Imputed credit costs were included in home market selling expenses and thus in constructed value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When imputed credit costs are part of home-market selling expenses, include them in CV; avoid double-counting by reducing interest expenses in company books as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments for differences in circumstances of sale
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust CV for differences in circumstances of sale in accordance with 19 CFR 353.56 (e.g., credit, warranty, technical service, after-sale expenses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make circumstance-of-sale adjustments to CV where appropriate and document specific categories adjusted for each respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for line‑item contract prices (no allocation if available)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's policy is to use line-item contract prices where they exist; the Department prefers not to engage in allocation of prices because allocations can introduce distortions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only accept alternative pricing methodologies (e.g., allocations based on cost) if line-item prices do not exist or the Department has no confidence in them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of internal documents (orders to plant) — limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal orders to the plant do not establish meaningful unit prices for customers and were not relied upon to determine individual MTP prices, except to break down line-item prices for certain movement charges and specification changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal orders may be used to allocate or break down charges only when no better contractual documentation exists or for movement/spec changes; they are less persuasive as customer-negotiated prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of spare parts in price and CV
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include price and/or cost of spare parts in the MTP price and/or constructed value where the price and/or cost of spare parts has been separately broken out in the sales documentation because they are not subject to the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where spare-part prices are not separately identified, use verified reported prices inclusive of spare parts as best information available; in some package sales allocate spare parts cost to individual pieces by COM under section 776(c) and include spare parts cost in CV where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of accessories/separately-identified items
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessories such as die tooling, load meter and load sensor that are separately identified in contractual documentation are not an 'integral part' of the press and are outside the scope of the investigation; segregate them from verified price and COM where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segregate separately-identified accessory items from subject merchandise for both price and cost analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of installation and installation supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Installation and related supervision expenses are treated as movement charges because disassembly and reassembly are necessary for shipment and delivery of large presses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deduct installation and installation supervision costs from verified MTP prices when included in the contract price; reclassify them from COM to movement charges as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of interest (FASB #34 / U.S. GAAP approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether interest expenses must be capitalized pursuant to FASB #34 by analyzing financing costs of work-in-process using company-specific interest rates and production periods to determine materiality; capitalize when financing costs are necessary for manufacturing, identifiable with production of specific presses, and material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use U.S. GAAP when foreign GAAP does not appropriately value costs; capitalize interest only for projects where capitalization is material — adjust general interest expenses accordingly; do not capitalize where immaterial or where production is routine and short-term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments to company CV/COM data where costs are misreported or omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust COM/CV to include or exclude costs where company cost accounting reports contain errors or misclassifications (e.g., include omitted costs, eliminate freight and packing from COM, include freight‑in, include scrap expenses, reclassify installation supervision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise cost of sales (COS) and the bases for G&A calculations to be consistent with methodologies used to calculate each product’s COM; include losses, idle depreciation, disposal of assets, special profits/losses related to labor when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of orders to plant / best information available when documentation lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: Where individual prices or costs are not available in sales documentation, the Department may use orders to the plant or other internal documents as best information available pursuant to 19 CFR 353.37 (e.g., when a package price includes non-subject merchandise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use orders to the plant to allocate package prices only when no contractual breakdown exists, and characterize this as best information available; document rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of sale — when basic terms agreed
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the date of the initial agreement (date when all basic terms are agreed upon) as the date of sale for large, custom-made merchandise; an internal order to the plant can be used when no prior documentation exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department favors establishing earlier date of sale for custom capital equipment to reflect commercial realities; minor post-agreement specification changes do not necessarily change date of sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification sampling practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department normally selects a sample of transactions for review at verification rather than verifying every reported transaction, especially where sales are numerous or complex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume unverified sales should be treated by default as highest margin or excluded; follow standard sampling and verification procedures and document coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of post‑shipment specification changes and related charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification changes that occur throughout production and after delivery (including those during installation) are common for these machines; any charge resulting from such changes has been included in the price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept charges stemming from oral agreements or post-shipment customer requests when they are part of the commercial process and evidenced in documentation or verified practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of commissions and discounts
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'commission' to the customer included in the price was treated as a discount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat amounts effectively reducing price to customer as discounts; use reported treatment and confirm via documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of formal purchase order prices where conflicts exist
rubrics_metrics.description: When internal notices of acceptance or other internal documents list prices that differ from the formal purchase order, the Department uses prices listed in the formal purchase order for analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on contractual sales documents (purchase orders, contracts) for price determination over narrative descriptions or internal drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of petitioner standing and burden on challengers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department presumes that a petitioner has standing (filed 'on behalf of' the domestic industry) until informed otherwise; the onus is on domestic industry members opposing the investigation to demonstrate that petitioner’s standing is in jeopardy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a respondent challenges standing, it must timely provide supporting factual information as required by 19 CFR 353.31(c)(2); absent such evidence, Department will not investigate standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and correction of factual information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's regulations permit submissions of factual information up until seven days before scheduled verification; corrections submitted at verification may be accepted if they are corrections of clerical errors and do not constitute a new questionnaire response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections that affect many data fields may still be acceptable if not introducing new methodologies or new sales; document telephone/letter requests and Department solicitations that prompted submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of averages vs specific data for supposedly identical units
rubrics_metrics.description: Averaging prices and costs for units claimed to be identical is inappropriate unless units are demonstrably identical; Department preference is to use line-item contract prices and specific cost data where available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If averaging is challenged, Department may use individual contract prices and product-specific COM and movement charges instead.
